CausalChain: Chronic hepatitis virus infection → increased IL‐6 in the tumor microenvironment → overactivation of STAT3 → upregulation of AFP, PD‐L1, and expansion of liver cancer stem cells → epigenetic silencing of SOCS3 removes negative feedback on IL‐6/STAT3 → sustained oncogenic signaling and drug resistance → targeted demethylation reactivates SOCS3 → inhibition of IL‐6/STAT3 signaling, reduced stemness and immune evasion
Hypothesis: Epigenetic reactivation of SOCS3 using targeted demethylating agents will restore its negative regulatory function on the IL-6/STAT3 pathway, thereby reducing liver cancer stem cell expansion, descending AFP and PD-L1 expression, and enhancing the sensitivity of hepatocellular carcinoma to STAT3-targeted therapies.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma is a multifaceted disease largely driven by persistent inflammation and cytokine signaling. One critical pathway involves IL‐6 induced activation of STAT3, which not only promotes tumor cell proliferation and drug resistance, but also supports the expansion of liver cancer stem cells and the establishment of an immunosuppressive microenvironment through upregulation of factors such as AFP and PD‐L1. Emerging evidence suggests that the negative feedback regulation provided by SOCS proteins, particularly SOCS3, is often compromised in HCC due to epigenetic silencing. In this context, reactivating SOCS3 expression via targeted epigenetic modulation may restore its inhibitory effect on the IL‐6/STAT3 cascade, thereby reducing cancer stem cell features, attenuating immune escape and ultimately enhancing the efficacy of existing STAT3 inhibitors. This study proposes an integrated approach to combine demethylating agents with IL‐6/STAT3 blockade as a novel therapeutic strategy against HCC.
